title: Carnival balls in the forties and fifties, with four trumpets and three trombones
summary: DeDroit says he led for Rex for about twenty years and describes staffing carnival-ball orchestras.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: You played carnival balls back in the twenties a lot?
I want to present you a little bit. Oh, thank you.
Were you playing carnival balls a lot back in the twenties?
You were too busy with your other work.

Yeah, but in the forties, I was the fifties. I was the official man for Rex for about twenty years. I played in the old carnival. I had thirty-five. I could make a living in the carnival season. Because you play a suburb dance, you know?

Do you think that had a lot to do with the fact that they had the carnival here? Do you think that has a lot to do with the fact that you had so much music in New Orleans because you had a big call for

the dance bands? During the carnival season, we sometimes had to engage men from the symphony, if they were available. There's always a shortage of men during the carnival season. Yes. And then some of them like big orchestras, you know, and some don't. But they like to make a splash, you know, or the captain does anyhow. And if you can talk, you've got a good line. For instance, if it was too light a ball and I had solos, like I told you, if we had played balls, bluett or something like that, I'd get Albert Curse, who was one of our fine, and I'd let him play the rock in the microphone when he got through and say, Al, you can go because they're not going to hear you. You know? The strings didn't count too much. French horns and trumpets, yeah, they got a chance, and the trombones. We used on average four trumpets and three trombones. The four trumpets, you see, they would spell one out because the grand march would last a long time.
You know how I used to- What years was this now, you're talking about all these four trumpets and three trombones?
